La réhabilitation vise à organiser sur un même site l'accueil des élèves du sud du territoire, soit 3 classes (1 maternelle et 2 élémentaires), une garderie périscolaire, une restauration scolaire avec un office de réchauffage, une cour oasis (actuellement bitumée) et un préau, ainsi que la mairie déléguée (bureaux et salle des mariages). La réhabilitation doit être conforme aux réglementations thermiques applicables, garantir une efficacité thermique été comme hiver, et satisfaire aux écoconditions régionales de Bourgogne Franche Comté, et aux conditions de financement fixées par les fonds verts, la DETR, l'Agence de l'eau, les CEE ou tout autre dispositif à venir. L'enveloppe prévisionnelle des travaux a été fixée à 2 500 000 € par le maître d'ouvrage, une réutilisation optimale des locaux existants et une sobriété d'exploitation ultérieure étant attendue. Le site est situé en zone ABF. Le chantier est à réaliser en site occupé.

It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or Invitation for Bid (IFB), nor is it a commitment by the U.S. Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. BACKGROUND & PURPOSE: The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) � Fort Knox, on behalf of the Department of the Army, Casualty and Mortuary Affairs Operations Division (CMAOD), is conducting market research to identify domestic manufacturers and suppliers capable of providing burial caskets and 100% domestically produced casket liners and interior upholstery fabrics compliant with the Berry Amendment (10 U.S.C. � 4862, formerly 10 U.S.C. � 2533a) and DFARS 252.225-7012. title: RFSO - Geotechnical and Hydrotechnical Engineering Services in Yukon (Up to 5)
description: This requirement is for the Department of Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada (CIRNAC). The Department of Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada (CIRNAC), Yukon Region is responsible for managing multiple contaminated sites in Yukon, including Type II abandoned mine sites. In order to meet CIRNAC’s project objectives, CIRNAC requires Hydrotechnical and Geotechnical Services to support ongoing care and maintenance, and advance remediation plans at multiple Type II mine sites and other DTA sites in the Yukon region. These sites have a variety of different geotechnical and hydrotechnical challenges associated with them. The specific scopes for supplying services to each site will vary according to each site’s needs. Works for each of these sites will be issued on an as-and-when requested basis, detailed in each call-up. The work under these SOAs is intended to be consistent with CIRNAC’s Contaminated Sites Management Policy whose objectives include: 1) to meet federal and departmental policy requirements and legal obligations regarding the management of contaminated sites; 2) to require that, where a suspected contaminated site has been identified, the site be assessed in a timely, consistent and cost effective manner; 3) to provide a scientifically valid, risk management based framework for setting priorities, planning, implementing and reporting on the management of contaminated sites; 4) to remediate, based on approved resource levels, all National Classification System (NCS) Class 1 contaminated sites in the North, and Class 1 and 2 contaminated sites on reserve, on a priority basis, unless it can be demonstrated that for a specific site an alternative form of management is appropriate; 5) to promote the social and economic benefits that may accrue to First Nations, Inuit and northerners when carrying out activities required by this policy; and 6) to promote the federal "polluter pay" principle. CIRNAC intends to establish Standing Offer Agreements (SOA) for multiple qualified Contractors to supply Geotechnical and Hydrotechnical Engineering Services for several abandoned mine sites throughout Yukon, including the following areas subject to Comprehensive Land Claims Agreements (CLCAs): 1. Carcross/Tagish First Nation Final Agreement 2. Champagne and Aishihik First Nation Final Agreement 3. First Nation of Nacho Nyak Dun Final Agreement 4. Kluane First Nation Final Agreement 5. Kwanlin Dün First Nation Final Agreement 6. Little Salmon/Carmacks First Nation Final Agreement 7. Selkirk First Nation Final Agreement 8. Ta'an Kwäch'än Council Final Agreement 9. Teslin Tlingit Council Final Agreement 10. Tr'ondëk Hwëch'in Final Agreement 11. Vuntut Gwitchin First Nation Final Agreement The intent is to award up to five (5) Standing Offer Agreements for a period from Standing Offer Award date to March 31, 2030, with two (2) one (1) year option periods. Level of Security: there are no security requirements applicable to this requirement.

title: Public Health Engineering Reviews – Alberta First Nation Projects (PSIB Set-Aside)
description: This requirement has been set aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB) and is open only to eligible Indigenous businesses. Indigenous Services Canada (ISC), Alberta Region, is seeking qualified engineering firms to provide public health engineering review and advisory services related to water, wastewater, and aquatic facility infrastructure projects in First Nations communities throughout Alberta. Services will be required on an as-and-when-requested basis and may include engineering reviews, risk assessments, site visits, stakeholder consultations, presentations, and the preparation of professional engineering reports in support of Environmental Public Health Services (EPHS). Canada reserves the right to exercise up to two (2) additional one-year option periods under the same terms and conditions. There are security requirements associated with this requirement. Bidders should consult the Request for Proposal (RFP) and related security documentation for complete details regarding the applicable security requirements and obligations.

title: Access Control and Intrusion Detection Services
description: The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) requires the provision of parts and labour (technical support, programming, installation, service, and maintenance) on an “as and when requested” basis for its Integrated Security System (ISS) at CRA locations across Canada. The CRA is considering the conversion of up to 51 sites currently using a combination of Digital Security Controls (DSC) Intrusion Detection Systems and Kantech Access Control systems to a unified Kantech Intrusion/Access Control platform. The site counts identified below represent the CRA’s current intended conversion plans for planning and estimation purposes only and do not constitute a commitment to convert any specific number of sites. The CRA requires the goods and services referenced above in the following regions: 1. National Capital Region (NCR) – up to 11 sites identified for potential conversion; 2. Ontario – up to 13 sites identified for potential conversion; 3. Quebec – up to 1 site identified for potential conversion; 4. Atlantic – up to 4 sites identified for potential conversion; and 5. Western – up to 22 sites identified for potential conversion. Bidders may submit a bid for one (1) or more Regions identified in this RFP. Only one (1) bid submission is required, regardless of the number of Regions for which the Bidder is submitting a bid. The Bidder's submission must clearly identify each Region for which it is proposing to provide the required goods and services. For each Region bid, the Bidder must provide all information required by this RFP, including any Region-specific technical information, resource information, and pricing, in the format prescribed in the bid solicitation documents. Requirement, project experience, certification, corporate qualification, or other bid components that are not Region-specific need only be submitted once and will be evaluated for all Regions included in the Bidder's submission. Bids for Multiple Regions: Requirements identified as Region-specific will be evaluated only for the applicable Region. Requirements that are not Region-specific will be evaluated once and will apply to all Regions included in the Bidder's submission. The CRA will evaluate each Region independently. Where a Bidder fails to meet a Region-specific requirement, the CRA may declare the bid non-responsive for that Region only. For greater certainty, a determination that a bid is non-responsive for one (1) Region will not, in itself, render the Bidder's submission non-responsive for any other Region for which a bid has been submitted, provided all applicable requirements for those Regions are met. The CRA intends to award up to five (5) contracts to fulfill this requirement. A Bidder may be awarded a contract for one (1) Region, multiple Regions, or all five (5) Regions. The period of the resulting contract(s) will be for three (3) firm years. The contract(s) will include four (4) irrevocable one-year options to extend the period of the contract(s). The contract(s) will also include provisions allowing the CRA to add, remove or modify products and sites. A bid must comply with the requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory evaluation criteria to be declared responsive. For each Region, the responsive bid with the highest combined rating of technical merit and price will be recommended for award of a contract. Each Region will be evaluated separately. Where the same Bidder is ranked first for multiple Regions, the CRA will award a single contract covering the Regions for which that Bidder is the highest-ranked responsive bidder. The Bid Compliance and Remedy Process (BCRP) defined in Part 4.2 will apply. Proposal documents and supporting information must be submitted in either English or French. Questions must be directed in writing to the contracting authority via email: Timothy.Berg@cra-arc.gc.ca Bids must be submitted by using the Connect service provided by the Canada Post Corporation. When responding, the proposal MUST be delivered to: Canada Revenue Agency Bid Receiving Unit BRUg@cra-arc.gc.ca Bids will not be accepted if emailed directly to this email address. This email address must be used to request that CRA open a Connect conversation, as detailed in Standard Instructions 2003. Bidders must not use their own licensing agreement for Connect to initiate a Connect conversation with CRA. The CRA reserves the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. There are security requirements associated with this requirement. For additional information, consult the bid solicitation document. The Federal Contractors Program (FCP) for employment equity applies to this procurement. This bid solicitation 1000536720/B cancels and supersedes previous bid solicitation number 1000536720/A dated 2026-03-27 with a closing of 2026-05-19 02:00 PM EDT. This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers and to Suppliers of an applicable trading partner. For additional information, consult the bid solicitation document. The CRA will include the following minimum work guarantees (all applicable taxes included) over the entire period of the resulting contract(s), which includes any exercised option periods, including any extension period thereof: 1. National Capital Region (NCR) – $100,000 CAD; 2. Ontario – $100,000 CAD; 3. Quebec – $50,000 CAD; 4. Atlantic – $50,000 CAD; and 5. Western – $100,000 CAD.

title: English to Inuktitut Translation Services
description: Limited to firms on the Inuit Firm Registry (IFR). This solicitation of offer is limited to offerors registered on the Inuit Firm Registry (IFR). Background Pursuant to section 46 of the Nunavut Act, the Auditor General is required to annually audit accounts and financial statements of the Government of Nunavut. As part of this requirement, the Office of the Auditor General of Canada (the OAG) produces a variety of documents, including the annual Nunavut report, that need to be translated from English into Inuktitut, in either the North or South Baffin dialect. Translated documents will also need to be edited and updated. Objective The objective of this procurement process is for the Contractor to provide timely, consistent and reliable English to Inuktitut translation and editing services for Nunavut reports, opening statements and communication products that will be presented by the OAG to the government of Nunavut. The OAG will also require translation or editing of other types of documents varying in length and topic throughout the year, including consolidated financial statements. The Contractor will perform all work from its own facilities. No travel is anticipated for the duration of the resulting contract. In executing the work, Contractor managed devices, tools and IT services will only be used when processing unprotected information. The OAG will provide a laptop computer and access to the OAG network when the work requires access to protected information. Term The period of the Contract is from 1-April-2027 to 31-March-2029 inclusive, with the option to extend the Contract for up to two (2) additional two-year periods.

title: IT Security Professional Services Under the Task-Based Services Supply Arrangement
description: Public Safety Canada requires task-based IT professional services to complete defined security assessment, authorization, architecture, testing, remediation-validation and incident-readiness packages for identified departmental systems, applications, cloud services, networks and technology initiatives. The Contractor will manage its personnel and methods of work and will remain responsible for producing complete and accepted deliverables. PS will identify systems, owners, security requirements and decision authorities; provide authorized access and available evidence; make risk decisions; and accept or reject deliverables. Contractor personnel will not be directed as employees of Canada. The Contractor must be capable of mobilizing and managing sufficient qualified resources to perform multiple concurrent Task Authorizations, where authorized by PS, without compromising agreed schedules, deliverable quality, required independence or security requirements. Only selected TBIPS SA Holders currently holding a TBIPS SA for Tier 1 in the National Capital Region under the EN578-170432 series of SAs are invited to compete. SA Holders may not submit a bid in response to this bid solicitation unless they have been invited to do so. However, should an uninvited SA Holder wish to be invited, it may contact the Contracting Authority to request an invitation at any time prior to five business days before the published bid closing date, and an invitation will be made to that SA Holder unless it would not be consistent with the efficient operation of the procurement system. In no circumstance will such an invitation require Canada to extend a bid closing date. Where additional invitations are made during the bid solicitation process, it may be that they are not reflected in a bid solicitation amendment.

title: Web-based Platform for Whole Building Life Cycle Analysis (WBLCA) and Embodied Carbon emissions in building and infrastructure construction
description: The National Research Council on behalf of the Government of Canada (GoC) and its’ Partners seek to procure a secure, scalable, bilingual web-based digital platform (“the platform”) to support the reporting, review, analysis, and visualization of embodied carbon emissions in building and infrastructure construction projects. This procurement includes the design, development, configuration, deployment and ongoing support of the platform. The solution will provide a centralized system that ensure consistent data collection, automated validation, and reporting in alignment with embodied carbon disclosure and reduction policies for buildings and infrastructure projects. At a minimum, the platform shall enable: - Intake of material and project specific embodied carbon submissions; - Import and export capabilities for compatible whole building Life Cycle Assessment (wbLCA) submission reports and raw data; - Dashboards and customizable reporting functions for internal analysis; and - The creation of an anonymized public dataset. The Platform MUST comply with Government of Canada security requirements for Protected A information and meet Canadian-based data residency requirements.

title: Kittilän lukion irtokalusteet
description: Kittilän lukion irtokalusteet Kittilän lukion peruskorjauksen yhteydessä uusitaan osa irtokalusteista. Kittilän kunta pyytää tarjouksia Kittilän lukion uusittavista irtokalusteista tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Kittilän lukion irtokalusteet kilpailutetaan käänteisenä kilpailutuksena eli ns. ranskalaisena urakkana. Tarjoukset annetaan kalustuksesta sekä suunnitteluprosessista. Valittavalle toimittajalle kuuluu irtokalustuksen kokonaissuunnittelu yhdessä tilaajatahon kanssa sekä kalusteiden toimittaminen laadittuja suunnitelmia noudattaen. Koko hankinnan (suunnitteluprosessi, kalusteet, kalusteiden toimitus-, kokoamis- ja asennuspalvelut sekä pakkausmateriaalien poiskuljetus) kokonaishinta on 150 000 € (alv 0 %). Tilaajalla on oikeus kasvattaa tai supistaa valitun toimittajan kanssa käytyjen neuvottelujen pohjalta hankinnan kokonaishintaa +/- 10 %. title: Karstulan koulukuljetusten hankintakonsultointi
description: Karstulan koulukuljetusten hankintakonsultointi Karstulan kunta valmistelee koulukuljetuspalvelujen kilpailuttamista kolmen vuoden sopimuskaudelle sekä kahdelle erilliselle optiovuodelle. Hankinnan kohteena on asiantuntijapalvelu, jossa valittava hankintakonsultti suunnittelee ja toteuttaa koulukuljetusten kilpailutuksen yhteistyössä Karstulan kunnan kanssa. Konsultin tulee huolehtia kilpailutusprosessin lainmukaisesta, tarkoituksenmukaisesta ja aikataulun mukaisesta toteuttamisesta. Tavoitteena on muodostaa koulukuljetuspalveluista toiminnallisesti selkeä ja kilpailukelpoinen hankintakokonaisuus, joka turvaa oppilaiden turvalliset ja toimivat kuljetukset, mahdollistaa keskenään vertailukelpoisten tarjousten antamisen, huomioi Karstulan kunnan alueelliset olosuhteet, edistää toimivien kuljetusmarkkinoiden muodostumista, sisältää selkeän ja hallittavan hinnoittelumallin, mahdollistaa sopimuksen tehokkaan seurannan sopimuskauden aikana sekä vähentää hankintamenettelyyn ja sopimuskauteen liittyviä oikeudellisia ja taloudellisia riskejä. Koulukuljetusten varsinaisen sopimuskauden suunniteltu alkamisajankohta on 1.8.2027. Sopimuskausi on kolme kouluvuotta sekä kaksi erillistä optiovuotta, päättyen näiden jälkeen 31.7.2032. Konsulttipalveluun tulee sisältyä seuraavat tehtäväkokonaisuudet: 1. koulukyytihankinnan ja sen osakokonaisuuksien suunnittelu 2. markkinakartoituksen ja tarvittaessa markkinavuoropuhelun suunnittelu ja toteuttaminen 3. tarjouspyynnön, palvelukuvauksen ja sopimusehtojen laatiminen 4. vertailuperusteiden, pisteytysmallin ja hinnoittelurakenteen muodostaminen 5. hankintailmoituksen ja tarjouspyynnön julkaiseminen HILMAssa 6. tarjoajien kysymyksiin annettavien vastausten valmistelu 7. tarjousten tarjouspyynnönmukaisuuden tarkastaminen 8. tarjousten vertailu ja vertailuasiakirjojen laatiminen 9. hankintapäätösesityksen valmistelu perusteluineen 10. hankintaoikaisujen, oikaisuvaatimusten ja muiden muutoksenhakutilanteiden käsittelyyn osallistuminen 11. sopimusasiakirjojen valmistelu ja sopimusten viimeistely. Koulukyytikilpailutuksessa laadittavan tarjouspyynnön tulee olla kirjallinen ja niin selkeä, että sen perusteella voidaan antaa keskenään vertailukelpoisia tarjouksia. Hankinnan kuvaus, soveltuvuusvaatimukset, vertailuperusteet, tarjousten määräaika ja voimassaolo ovat tarjouspyynnön keskeisiä tietoja.,

title: Intrinsic Market Resilience (IMR)
description: The evolution of markets from physical trading floors to interconnected, electronic venues has introduced new speed, transparency, and efficiency, but has also created new attack surfaces and systemic risks. Modern markets, which host trading for everything from equities and bonds to energy and cloud computing resources, can be manipulated in ways unanticipated by their designers. The 2010 United States Equity market "flash crash" and the 2000-2001 California energy crisis demonstrated how weaknesses in a market's public interfaces could have dramatic consequences. Similar design issues in today's complex, interacting market systems could be used to cause economic damage, which the IMR program technology seeks to prevent. The IMR program aims to develop repair methods to protect essential economic sectors against devastating attacks that exploit the public interfaces of modern markets. Current legal and regulatory protections focus on deterring profit-seeking manipulation and ensuring compliance, but they do not sufficiently protect markets from adversaries aiming simply to cause disruption. The IMR program seeks to address this gap by developing the tools to automatically model market designs, identify hidden weaknesses, and recommend and analyze repairs on the market models to make markets fundamentally more resilient to attack. IMR aims to combine Large Language Model (LLM)-based automation with rigorous modeling and analysis to identify remediations for market weaknesses. The program will develop formal notations to precisely describe how markets operate and coordinate, creating machine-analyzable models from informal descriptions like regulatory filings and technical specifications. Against these models, IMR will formulate and assess "resilience conjectures� - mathematical statements about desirable market properties, such as the inability for actors to manipulate prices without risking loss. By automatically analyzing these conjectures, the program aims to prove that a market design is resilient in specific ways or, if it is not, to generate a counterexample that illustrates a concrete weakness. These counterexamples will then be used to refine the conjectures and, ultimately, to recommend and confirm specific repairs to the market's design. This approach is intended to provide a capability to protect U.S. markets against adversaries who wish to cause chaos, ensuring the stability of both civilian and military critical resources that rely on modern market mechanisms.

description: La présente consultation est lancée par l'établissement support du Groupement Hospitalier de Territoire (GHT) Drôme Ardèche Vercors conformément aux dispositions de l'article R.6132-16 du Code de la santé publique. Elle concerne les établissements parties suivants : CH de Valence, Groupement hospitalier Portes de Provence, Hôpitaux Drôme Nord, CH d'Ardèche Méridionale, CH Drôme Vivarais, CH Privas Ardèche, CH Crest, CH Villeneuve de Berg, CH Intercommunal Vercors Isère, CH Die, CH Cévennes Ardéchoises, CH Tournon, CH Bourg-Saint-Andéol-Viviers, CH Lamastre, CH Nyons, CH Buis-les-Baronnies, CH Le Cheylard, CH Vallon Pont d'Arc, GCS BIH), GCS RND) --- Contexte de la procédure : Afin de disposer d'une capacité de fourniture performante, la Fonction Achat Mutualisé du GHT Drome Ardèche a décidé d'utiliser la technique d'achat des &quot;systèmes d'acquisition dynamique&quot; (SAD) pour répondre à ses besoins ponctuels et spécifiques. L'objectif est de répondre au juste besoin des établissements dans des délais de livraison raisonnable, sans rupture d'approvisionnement. --- Forme du contrat : Le marché est un marché de fournitures passé selon la technique d'achat du système d'acquisition dynamique au sens du 4° de l'article L2125-1 du Code de la commande publique. Il est soumis aux dispositions des articles R.2162-37 à R.2162-51 du code de la commande publique. La procédure est entièrement électronique, dès la publication de l'avis de mise en oeuvre du système jusqu'à son expiration. Par nature, le système d'acquisition dynamique est multi-attributaire. Les modalités de remise en concurrence et d'exécution des marchés spécifiques sont prévues à l'article « Marchés spécifiques » du CCAP. title: St. Lucie South Jetty Repair Industry Day
description: This announcement constitutes a Special Notice. This announcement seeks information from industry and will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SPECIAL NOTICE. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. This is a SAVE-THE-DATE special notice for an industry day event on 07 December 2026 at 10:00 AM EST. All interested Offerors are required to access SAM.gov for future updates. Please view registration information and details below. The presentation slides and list of attendees will be made available and posted to the subject special notice on SAM.gov after the conclusion of the event. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Jacksonville District will be holding an Industry Day event to gauge the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of various members of the Construction Community, to include Small Businesses. This event will provide information and obtain feedback from interested Offerors prior to issuance of the official solicitation. This requirement is for fiscal year (FY) 2027 award. NAICS Code 237990: Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction Small Business Standard: $45 million Price Target Range: $25 - $50 million Estimated Period of Performance: 730 calendar days Project Background Project Title: St. Lucie South Jetty Rehabilitation Interagency, Martin County, Florida. Project Description: The work consists of rehabilitation of the head structure of the South Jetty at St. Lucie Inlet. This includes a rebuilt rounded head structure and head-to-trunk transition with a marine mattress foundation and toe protection stones. Rehabilitation will require substantial moving and manipulation of both new and existing stones to obtain the required interlocking. The reworking of existing stones is only for incorporation of new stone. The retrieval of existing stone outside of the design template will not be required and is not part of the necessary rework of existing stone. The originally constructed South Jetty is approximately 1,320 feet in length with a crest height of 5.5 feet NAVD88. The crest width is 10 feet and the north and south slopes of the structure slope at 1V:2H. There is an asphalt walkway approximately 1,090 feet in length that runs along the existing jetty crest, terminating eastward at approximately Station 12+00 as shown on the approved permit drawings. Manipulation of stone along the crest may be necessary while completing the required work along the side slopes. The asphalt walkway will need to be removed within the repair area as necessary as work progresses. Any asphalt sections removed, or damaged such that they need to be removed, must be transported and properly disposed of off-site, and will not need to be replaced. Project Information Scope of Work: The proposed work includes rehabilitation of the head of the south jetty structure (the seaward-most 400 to 500 feet) by restabilizing the structure foundation and placing a second layer of large armor stone. The proposed scope includes: Excavating the existing bed material to place a widened marine mattress foundation, expanding the current structure footprint up to 85 feet on the jetty centerline as shown on the approved permit drawings; Placing 9- to 15-ton toe protection stones to form the structure foundation and provide scour protection; Removing and disposing of the remaining asphalt walkway and other debris off-site; Repairing the existing core and reworking the single layer of armor stone, as needed; and, Placing a second layer of 9- to 15-ton armor stone to stabilize the structure. Overview of Construction Staging and Access Requirements: Clearing of access routes and staging areas may be required. Any areas that are disturbed during construction are to be restored to pre-construction conditions or better once jetty rehabilitation work is completed. Expansion and/or improvements of access routes may be required. Maximum limits of access routes and staging areas are shown on the approved permit drawings. Additional Environmental Considerations: Construction will be permitted all year round and confined to daylight hours only. Construction that occurs during turtle and shorebird nesting seasons or has the potential to impact other Endangered Species Act (ESA) Protected Species, is subject to environmental restrictions and monitoring requirements. Refer to Table 1 under the Attachments for a list of protected species. Access from the water is allowed, but material cannot be dredged outside of the construction limits. All material excavated must pass through a 2-inch screen prior to use as backfill around the jetty structure or on the beach. All screened material must be disposed of off site. Excavated material may be used to build up the east staging area within the limits shown on the approved permit drawings. After jetty rehabilitation work is complete, the staging area must be graded to the beach fill template and native vegetation restored as shown on the approved permit drawings. Requests for Information: Industry is asked to consider the following questions and provide input at the Industry Day: Company/Contractor name, address, point of contact, phone number and e-mail address. Does the Contractor plan to submit a proposal for this contract? Describe the proposed construction methods and equipment needed to rehabilitate the jetty. Address, at a minimum, excavation of existing grade, maintaining open excavation areas, debris removal, and installation of marine mattresses and armor stone. Would temporary earth-retention or water-control measures, such as a cofferdam or similar system, be required to complete the work? Would dewatering be completed if this is the proposed construction methodology? If a cofferdam or other earth-retention system that also excludes all swimming ESA-listed species is not proposed, describe the measures that would be used to prevent the swimming ESA-listed species from entering the active work area during construction, including proposed turtle deterrent measures. ESA-listed species present in the area are included in Table 1 under the Attachments. Describe the turbidity control measures that would be incorporated into the proposed construction methodology. If it is not feasible, describe the limitation or restrictions for why not. What safety constraints or hazards could limit the practicality of potential construction methods? What temporary protections or operational measures would be needed to perform the work during winter months, given the inlet�s elevated coastal conditions during that period? Event Date: Monday, 07 December 2026 at 10:00 AM EST Event Location: 2401 SE Monterey Rd, Stuart, FL 34996 *Everyone will need to have a driver's license or id to get through security. Contact Info: Jim LaGrone, Project Manager James.W.Lagrone@usace.army.mil 904-521-2086 If you cannot attend in person: Link Meeting: https://www.microsoft.com/EN-US/MICROSOFT-TEAMS/JOIN-A-MEETING Meeting ID: 993 391 786 289 Passcode: kR3Zt9F8 Join by phone: 601-262-2433 Phone conference ID: 450 517 165# Event Schedule: Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the above project are invited to submit a capabilities statement, a response to the questionnaire on this Special Notice and any questions you have for the Government ahead of the breakout session by no later than December 04, 2026, at 1:00 PM, EST. All responses under this Special Notice shall be sent via email to Nicole Batista-Cruz at Nicole.M.Batista-Cruz@usace.army.mil, and Ruth Rodriguez at ruth.c.rodriguez@usace.army.mill. Your email subject line should be addressed as "St. Lucie South Jetty Repair Industry Day Registration (Company Name) - W912EP-27-Z-1CUE " to ensure the request is handled in a timely manner. All interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the above project are also invited to request a breakout session with the Govern

title: Q702--St. Louis JC Bed Tower IOTA IDIQ
description: Department of Veterans Affairs Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) October 6, 2026 PRESOLICITATION NOTICE Initial Outfitting, Transition and Activation (IOTA) Services for the St. Louis John Cochran Veterans Affairs Medical Center, New Bed Tower. 100% SDVOSB SET ASIDE This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice that the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) intends to solicit quotes to provide non-personal IOTA Services for the St. Louis John Cochran Veterans Affairs Medical Center, New Bed Tower. This requirement supports VA's mission by providing contractor services to help support the activation. The intended contract type is an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with an eight (8) year ordering period. The VA St. Louis Health Care System - John Cochran Division (VA STLHCS-JC), located at 915 North Grand Boulevard, St. Louis, Missouri, is part of a two-division health care system that also includes the Jefferson Barracks VAMC approximately 18 miles south of the John Cochran campus. These facilities serve Veterans in metropolitan St. Louis, Missouri, southwestern Illinois, and the broader Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 15 service area. The John Cochran campus is in a highly constrained urban setting in midtown St. Louis. The existing hospital infrastructure includes Building 1, constructed in 1953, and the Clinical Addition constructed in the mid-1980s. The campus requires modernization to address functional adjacency, physical security/force protection, aging infrastructure, seismic compliance, parking, and clinical capacity concerns. The Department of Veterans Affairs Office of Construction and Facilities Management (CFM), VA St. Louis Health Care System, and the Kansas City District (NWK) U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) are partnering to provide new and replacement facilities for the John Cochran Division. The John Cochran Major Project will relocate inpatient functions to a new seismically compliant Bed Tower, add new functionality, improve departmental adjacencies, replace aging utility infrastructure, and address physical security requirements. The John Cochran Major Project includes campus-wide expansion. Planned new facilities include, but are not limited to, parking garages, a Central Utility Plant, the Bed Tower, an Engineering/Administration building, a motor pool building, and supporting structures. The project includes more than 700,000 net usable square feet of new space. Clinical and administrative services anticipated to be supported include surgery, radiology, pharmacy, surgical services, spinal cord injury inpatient and rehabilitation services, emergency services, engineering, police, nutrition and food services, dialysis, and additional services as refined by the Government-approved program and design documents. This requirement will be set-aside 100% for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) using FAR Part 12 and 37. To be eligible for an SDVOSB set aside under VA s Veterans First Contracting Program, SDVOSBs must: be verified by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) as SDVOSB (see https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ for details) and meet the small business size standard for NAICS 541614. The solicitation is anticipated to be posted on Contract Opportunities for download on or about 29 October 2026. Potential offerors are advised that there may be truncated response time on the solicitation that will follow this Pre-Solicitation notice. Anticipated closing date of the solicitation will be 7 December 2026. Solicitation initial posting date and the closing date are subject to change as necessary. The first Task Order (TO#1 Project Management and Pre-Planning Support) will be included as part of the solicitation and awarded concurrently with the IDIQ. Quotes will be required for both the IDIQ and Task Order #1. Any questions for this Pre-solicitation notice should be sent via e-mail to Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov. No telephone requests/questions will be accepted. This Pre-Solicitation notice does not constitute a request for quotes. P.O.C: Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov, Contracting Officer

title: Renovate Building 1203-DOAS/AHU and Fire Suppression Water System, March Air Reserve Base, California
description: This solicitation is for construction services required for HVAC and Fire Suppression systems repair of Building 1203 at March Air Reserve Base, CA. This is an Invitation For Bid, sealed bid procurement. The solicitation notice will be posted to SAM.gov 4 November 2026 by Close of Business.The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Louisville District hereby issues an Invitation for Bid (IFB), Solicitation No. W912QR27BA004, to renovate Building 1203-DOAS/AHU and Fire Suppression Water System, March Air Reserve Base, California. A description of the construction project is as follows:This work consists of, but is not limited to, installing a new Dedicated Outside Air System (DOAS) air handling unit, the replacement of Air Handling Unit (AHU-02) and the replacement of the existing waterline that ties the main waterline to Building 1203. The distance of waterline to be replaced is estimated to be 100-ft. Additional site-work will include a larger housekeeping pad, larger equipment access platform, and larger landscaped enclosure to accommodate the additional DOAS air handling unit. New outside air supply and return ductwork will be incorporated leading from the DOAS unit to the rooms served by AHU-02 providing direct-to-room ventilation. The Contract Duration is 500 calendar days from Administrative Notice to Proceed.TYPE OF CONTRACT AND NAICS: This IFB is intended to result in the award of one Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. The North American Industrial Classification System Code (NAICS) for this effort is 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction.TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside.DISCUSSIONS: The Government intends to award without discussions but reserves the right to conduct discussion should it be deemed in the be interest of the Government.CONSTRUCTION MAGNITUDE: The magnitude of this construction project is anticipated to be between $1 million and $5 million.REGISTRATIONS: Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the following database: System for Award Management (SAM): Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the SAM database at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for a Government contract award. If the Offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity shall have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. If at the time of award an Offeror is not actively and successfully registered in the SAM database, the Government reserves the right to award to the next prospective Offeror. POINT-OF-CONTACT: The point-of-contact for this procurement is Rachael McClellan, Rachael.L.McClellan@usace.army.mil. PARTNERING WITH US: https://www.usace.army.mil/Business-With-Us/Partnering/Information regarding the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers process for settling requests for equitable adjustments and duration goals to achieve defeminization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts can be found by going to https://www.usace.army.mil/Business-With-Us/Partnering/ and then clicking on: View FFP Contract Changes Playbook Here.

The proposed scope includes: Excavating the existing bed material to place a widened marine mattress foundation, expanding the current structure footprint up to 85 feet on the jetty centerline as shown on the approved permit drawings; Placing 9- to 15-ton toe protection stones to form the structure foundation and provide scour protection; Removing and disposing of the remaining asphalt walkway and other debris off-site; Repairing the existing core and reworking the single layer of armor stone, as needed; and, Placing a second layer of 9- to 15-ton armor stone to stabilize the structure. Overview of Construction Staging and Access Requirements: Clearing of access routes and staging areas may be required. Any areas that are disturbed during construction are to be restored to pre-construction conditions or better once jetty rehabilitation work is completed. Expansion and/or improvements of access routes may be required. Maximum limits of access routes and staging areas are shown on the approved permit drawings. Additional Environmental Considerations: Construction will be permitted all year round and confined to daylight hours only. Construction that occurs during turtle and shorebird nesting seasons or has the potential to impact other Endangered Species Act (ESA) Protected Species, is subject to environmental restrictions and monitoring requirements. Refer to Table 1 below for a list of protected species. Access from the water is allowed, but material cannot be dredged outside of the construction limits. All material excavated must pass through a 2-inch screen prior to use as backfill around the jetty structure or on the beach. All screened material must be disposed of off site. Excavated material may be used to build up the east staging area within the limits shown on the approved permit drawings. After jetty rehabilitation work is complete, the staging area must be graded to the beach fill template and native vegetation restored as shown on the approved permit drawings. title: Jäänhoito- ja latukoneiden huolto- ja korjauspalvelut 2027 (2030)
description: Oulun Tilapalvelut -liikelaitos pyytää tarjousta Jäänhoito- ja latukoneiden huolto- ja korjauspalveluista sopimuskaudelle 1.1.2027 - 31.12.2027. Mahdolliset optiokaudet vuosi kerrallaan ajanjaksolle 1.1.2028 - 31.12.2030. Tilaaja ilmoittaa optioiden luopumisesta 3kk ennen optiokauden alkamista, muutoin optiot tulevat käyttöön ja voimaan automaattisesti. Hankinnasta perustetaan puitejärjestely. Osa-alueen etusijajärjestys määräytyy vertailun kokonaispistemäärän perusteella. Eniten pisteitä saanut tarjoaja sijoittuu ensimmäiseksi. Huoltopalvelun osa-alueilla vertailuperusteena on hinta. Akuuttikorjauksen osa-alueilla vertailuperusteina ovat hinta 95 pistettä ja samaa laitemerkkiä koskevan huoltopalvelun tarjoaminen 5 pistettä. Palveluntuottajia valitaan enintään kaksi per osa-alue. Varsinainen palveluntuottaja ja varasijalle toinen. Mikäli hyväksyttäviä tarjouksia saadaan vain yksi, tilaaja voi perustaa puitejärjestelyn kyseiseen osa-alueeseen yhden toimittajan kanssa. Kaikkia osa-alueita (kaikki jäänhoitokonemerkit) ei tarvitse tarjota. Tuntihintojen ja pisteytyskriteerien tarjoaminen tapahtuu "hankinnat kohdan kriteerit" kohdassa. Huolto- ja tuntihinnat tarjotaan per laitemerkki erikseen. Lisäpisteitä saa, jos samaan merkkiin tarjotaan sekä huolto- että korjauspalvelua. Tällöin korjauspalvelun kohdalla tulee merkitä ”kyllä” tarjottu huoltopalvelua. Tarjottuun hinta on esitettävä arvonlisäverottomina (alv 0 %) nettohintoina, jotka sisältävät kaikki palvelun tuottamisesta aiheutuvat kustannukset mahdolliset kilometri, matka-, majoitus-, päiväraha-, ylityö- sekä toimitus-, laskutus- ja toimistokulut mukaan lukien. Matka-ajasta saa laskuttaa tarjouslomakkeella ilmoitettua tuntihintaa enintään yhdeltä henkilöltä. Matka-aika lasketaan lyhintä tavanomaista ajoreittiä pitkin Oulun kaupungin hallinnolliselta rajalta tai toimittajan Oulun kaupungin alueella sijaitsevasta vakituisesta toimipisteestä työkohteeseen ja takaisin. Erillisiä kilometri-, päiväraha-, majoitus- tai muita matkakuluja ei saa laskuttaa. Mikäli 1. sijoittunut ei pysty /on estynyt ottamasta työtä vastaan, tilaaja käyttää 2. sijoittunutta palveluntarjoajaa. Valittu palveluntuottaja ei voi ilman perusteltua syytä kieltäytyä vastaanottamasta työtilausta ja perustelut annetaan kirjallisesti esim. sähköpostin välityksellä. Huoltopalvelun ja ei-kiireellisen korjauksen vasteaika arkisin on 5 vrk. (työn vastaanotto ja sen aloitus). Akuuttikorjauspalvelun vasteaika arkisin ja viikonloppuisin on 1 vrk. (työn vastaanotto ja sen aloitus). Töitä saavat tilata ainoastaan tilaajan nimeämät yhteyshenkilöt (työnjohtajat), jotka määrittelee erikseen työtä tilatessaan, onko työ huolto- vai ei-kiireellistä tai akuuttikorjaustyötä. Huoltopalvelu suoritetaan merkkivalmistajan huolto-ohjelman mukaisesti ja tarjoajalla tulee olla käytössään merkkivalmistajan tarjoamat ja ylläpitämät diagnostiikkatyökalut tai valmistajan hyväksymät tai teknisesti vastaavat. Huollot toteutetaan pääsääntöisesti kauden ulkopuolella yleensä touko- syyskuun välisenä ajankohtana. Huolto tapahtuu tilaajan tarjoamissa tiloissa Oulun talousalueella (Kanta Oulu, Haukipudas, Kiiminki, Ylikiiminki ja Yli-Ii). Akuuttikorjauspalvelu tehdään tilaajan tilaamana ennalta arvaamattomien vikatilanteiden osalta. Korjaustyö on akuuttia, välitöntä ja välttämätöntä korjausta, johon tulee reagoida sopimuksen mukaisella kiireellisellä aikataululla. Korjaukset tehdään pääsääntöisesti koneiden käyttöpaikalla maastossa. Huolto- ja korjauspalvelussa hankittavien varaosien tulee olla uusia ja alkuperäislaatuisia. Materiaaleille ja varaosille on voimassa kiinteä kateprosentti, joka on 5%. Alkuperäiset varaosien ostolaskut tulee liittää tilaajalle toimitettavaan laskuun mukaan. Tilaajalla on oikeus tarpeen mukaan tilata erikseen yksittäisiä varaosia ja tarvikkeita palveluntuottajalta omaan kalustoon. Tilaaja voi poistaa / lisätä huolto- ja korjauspalvelun piiriin kuuluvaa kalustoa vuosittain. Tilaaja informoi muutoksista palveluntuottajaa. Mikäli Tilaajalle tulee uusia tarjouspyynnössä mainitsemattomia laitemerkkejä, voi tilaaja pyytää puitesopimuskumppaneilta minikilpailutuksen kautta tarjoushinnat uudelle laitemerkille. Tarjoukset eivät saa sisältää omia ehtoja. Hankintayksikkö ei sitoudu mihinkään hankintamäärään. Tilaajalla on oikeus hylätä kaikki tarjoukset perustellusta syystä. title: USACE SPK DBB Construction - Calaveras Wastewater Treatment Plant Improvements - Copperopolis, CA
description: This Sources Sought Notice is being issued for market research purposes to determine the availability, capability, and interest of small business firms for a potential Government requirement. NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE; requests for the solicitation will go unanswered. No award will be made from this Notice. Responses will be used to determine potential acquisition strategies, understand current market capabilities, and to gain knowledge of potential sources. The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Sacramento District (SPK) anticipates a potential requirement for Design-Bid-Build (DBB) construction services to conduct Copper Cove Wastewater Treatment Plant (CCWTP) Improvements in collaboration with the Calaveras County Water District (CCWD) in Calaveras County, California (CA). The project is anticipated to include installation of a new continuous backwash filtration system to replace an existing filter system; electrical improvements to include upgrading the existing PG&E service size to the main switchboard located in the Control Building, installing a new transformer, raceways, metering panel, new Motor Control Center (MCC), and associated wiring and components; interconnection with a pre-existing CCWD-installed suspended air floatation (SAF) filter pretreatment system; installation of a new continuous backwash filter system to include excavation, shoring, and backfill for a partially buried cast-in-place concrete tank with three (3) equipped filter cells (modules), air control panel, grating and handrailing over the filter cells and feed channel; inlet and outlet piping, valves, and connection to existing ultraviolet (UV) inlet piping; and power and control tie-ins. The project is also anticipated to include construction of a new masonry compressor building on a concrete slab foundation, housing a duplex air compressor with space for an additional unit, along with appurtenant equipment on the compressed air piping including a refrigerated air dryer, oil-water separator, and air filter; a new wet well and submersible pump station to include a new buried precast wet well with an adjacent valve vault housing a duplex submersible pump station, valves and appurtenances, piping, and power control conduits constructed adjacent to the new SAF to convey filter backwash waste flow to the SAF. Finally, the project is anticipated to include demolition and disposal of the existing adsorption clarifier and mixed media filter equipment, dewatering of sludge handling facility solids in three (3) containerized, polymer-assisted gravity sludge dewatering systems that will be positioned on a concrete pad with containment walls and drainage systems to capture drained water and return it to Pond 6 through three (3) quick coupler hose connection points (one (1) per bin), and all associated yard pipe modifications to connect the new components to the existing WWTP, generally buried in suitable native or engineered backfill at depths of approximately three (3) to ten (10) feet of cover. The potential requirement may result in a firm-fixed-price construction solicitation issued approximately December 2026. If solicited, the Government intends to award the anticipated requirement by approximately March 2027. The Government estimates that construction of the anticipated requirement can be completed within three-hundred-sixty-five (365) calendar days from Contractor receipt of the Notice to Proceed. Work may also be impacted by bird nesting season, which runs from 1 February through 31 August. If market conditions indicate the estimated period of performance may be unrealistic, Respondents are encouraged to provide specific information (such as known equipment lead times or other timeline concerns) for Government consideration when responding to this Sources Sought Notice. The Government currently estimates the target price range for the anticipated project may be between $5,000,000.00 and $10,000,000.00. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code identified for the anticipated requirement is 237110, Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction. The small business size standard for the NAICS, as established by the U.S. Small Business Administration, is $45,500,000.00 annual revenue. The Product or Service Code (PSC) for the anticipated requirement is Y1PD, Construction of Waste Treatment and Storage Facilities. If there is a reasonable expectation that two (2) or more responsible small business concerns under the NAICS can provide the anticipated services, the Contracting Officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. If competition is set-aside for competition limited to small businesses, Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting (Deviation), requires that construction small business Contractors self-perform at least twenty-five percent (25%) of the cost of the contract, excluding the cost of materials. If no set aside is made, the requirement is competed with full and open competition, and the awarded Contractor is not a small business, the Contractor may be required to self-perform a percentage of work if required in the solicitation. Contractors with the skill, capabilities, workload capacity, and ability to obtain bonding to complete the project described above (either through self-performance and/or Subcontractor management) are invited to provide capability statements to the primary point of contact listed below. Other than small businesses are also encouraged to submit Capability Statements. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Responses must be limited to ten (10) 8.5 x 11 inch pages with a minimum font size of point 10. Please provide the following information: 1) Company name, System for Award Management (SAM) Unique Entity Identification (UEID) number or Employer Identification Number (EIN), address, point of contact name, contact phone number, contact e-mail address, and statement identifying whether the company employs union or non-union workers. 2) Experience and capability to complete contracts of similar magnitude and complexity to the potential requirement, including at least three (3) examples of comparable work performed within the past six (6) years. Each example should include a brief description of the project, description of the work performed (identification of self-performance and/or Subcontractor management), customer name, customer satisfaction, timeliness of performance, dollar value of the project, and whether there were any challenges experienced during the project (delays, investigations, health and safety issues, labor shortages, management / organizational issues, etc.). 3) Business size and socioeconomic type for the applicable NAICS (ex: Woman-Owned Small Business, Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), certified Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone), 8(a) Participant, small business, or other than small business (large business)). 4) Bonding capability (in the form of a Surety letter). Please submit all capabilities statements, information, brochures, and/or marketing material as one (1) document, limited to the page quantity above. Responses will not be considered an offer, proposal, or bid for any solicitation that may result from this Notice. Moreover, responses will not restrict the Government to an acquisition approach. This Notice is for information and planning purposes only. Respondents will not be notified of the results of any review conducted or the capability statements received. Please provide responses and/or questions by e-mail to the Contract Specialist, Costa Laliotitis, at (Constantinos.Laliotitis@usace.army.mil) by 0800 / 8:00 a.m. Pacific Time on Monday, 7 December 2026. Please include the Sources Sought Notice number W9123827X1CHG in the e-mail subject line.

title: PM Support Contract
description: THIS NOTICE IS FOR SOURCES SOUGHT ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR INVITATION FOR BID. SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS AND DRAWINGS ARE NOT AVAILABLE. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. Respondents will not be notified of the Sources Sought results. This Sources Sought is issued for the sole purpose of conducting Market Research in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Part 10 and identifying vendors capable of fulfilling Agency needs. USACE personnel may contact firms responding to this announcement to clarify a responder�s capabilities and other matters as part of this market research process. The tracking number for this announcement is W912P827SSA001. Please include in your firm�s response to this Sources Sought request. USACE anticipates a requirement under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 541330, Engineering Services. The Government contemplates and unrestricted procurement with a reserve for Small Business concerns for a Firm Fixed Price Multiple Award Task Order Contracts (MATOC) for MVN Civil Works Program & Project Management Support Services. The requirement: USACE New Orleans District seeks responsive and responsible small business offerors who shall provide services for the Civil Works Program & Project Management Support Services for efforts related to the water resources programs in southern Louisiana including USACE Civil Works Programs. Services include project management/planning support, development of project performance reports, updates to program management plans, project scheduling input, project cost support, presentation development, interagency agreement development /updates, project drawings and maps, other project reports, and monthly status reports. Qualifications: The contractor shall have the capability of providing project management and planning support, development of project performance reports, updates to Project/Program Management Plans (PMPs), project scheduling analysis, project cost tracking support, development of project performance reports, project cost tracking support, development of briefings and presentations, interagency agreement support, mapping and spatial project visual support, and monthly contract status reports. The contractor shall formulate flood risk management, navigation, and ecosystem restoration plans supported by quantitative benefits analysis. The contractor shall conduct studies, inventory and forecast of problems and opportunities, formulation of measures and alternative plans, evaluation and comparison of alternatives plans, evaluation and comparison of alternatives, calculation and comparison of monetized and non-monetized benefits. The contractor shall prepare documents such as federal interest determination, reconnaissance, feasibility, post-authorization and other reports, including cultural resources studies and reports, and hazardous, toxic, and radiological waste (HTRW) investigations, National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and /or other environmental quality documents. The contractor shall document water and wastewater issues as necessary to develop master plan level documents for environmental infrastructure, PAS, SJ, CAP, and other programs as required. The contractor shall develop ecosystems habitat surveys, endangered or threatened species surveys, wetlands assessments using standard State of Louisiana methods in coopetition with other Federal and State agencies, modeling, and mitigation and monitoring plans. The contractor shall coordinate with Corps, non-Federal partners, and other stakeholders to document existing flood damage problems, historical flood maps, potential ecosystem restoration, and recreation problems and opportunities within the study area. The contractor shall coordinate with Corps and non-Federal partners to document required excavation permits, utility easements, rights-of-way, and other project-related requirements shortly after exercising this contract. The contractor shall document all or part of NEPA and/or other environmental documents, including, but not limited to, Biological and HTRW assessments, Environmental Assessments (EA), and Environmental Impact Statements (Els's). Potential sources are requested to submit: A Capability statement identifying current or previous contracts, scope and magnitude of Program & Project Management Support Services. Please note: All contractors doing business with the Federal Government must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database. The website for registration Potential firms MUST have an active record in the System for Award Management (SAM) database to be considered for award. Include in your capabilities package: your company's name, address, Point of Contact with corresponding phone number, e-mail address, Unique Entity Identifier Number, Cage Code, and System for Award Management profile which displays the expiration date. Proof of small business size must also be included. All interested firms are invited to submit a capability statement of no more than five (5) pages back and front, and no smaller than 12-point Times New Roman font. The capability statement should demonstrate the interested firm's understanding, capability, approach, qualifications, and past experience as it relates to the work stated within this Source Sought notice. title: Request for Information (RFI) Enhanced Maritime Biological Detection (EMBD) Identification Subsystem (IDS)
description: The Joint Product Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Sensing (JPdM CS), under the Joint Project Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Integrated Early Warning (JPM CBRN IEW), under the Portfolio Management Executive Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense (PME CBRND) within the Department of War (DoW), is conducting market research to identify potential industry sources capable of providing a Biological Warfare Agent (BWA) identification capability for integration into the U.S. Navy's Enhanced Maritime Biological Detection (EMBD) system. As a backward-compatible replacement for the Joint Biological Point Detection System (JBPDS) Identifier, the EMBD Identification Subsystem (IDS) automatically provides confirmatory identification of Biological Warfare Agents (BWAs) in liquid samples. In operation, the EMBD Collector gathers the sample externally and routes it to the IDS via the EMBD Fluid Transfer System (FTS). Please see the attached formal Request for Information (RFI) for full details.

title: Calcasieu Bar River Channel, Pascagoula Harbor, and Panama City Harbor Maintenance Dredging
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC) requires a contract to provide maintenance dredging for (3) dredging projects. The areas of consideration for these dredging services are: Calcasieu Bar River Channel, Pascagoula Harbor, and Panama City Harbor.Calcasieu River Bar Channel: Work for the Calcasieu River Bar Channel will require one fully crewed and equipped self-propelled trailing suction type hopper dredge. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -45ft MLLW and place dredged material into the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Sites (ODMDS).Pascagoula Harbor: Work for the Pascagoula Harbor maintenance dredging will require a hopper dredge. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -46 ft MLLW and place dredged material in the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Site (ODMDS). Dredged material shall be placed within Pascagoula ODMDS. The transport distance to the designated placement area varies depending on dredge assignment but typically is within 3-5 miles of the dredge cut.Panama City Harbor: Work for the Panama City Harbor maintenance dredging will require a medium to small hopper. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -40 ft MLLW and place dredged material within channel adjacent to the entrance jetty. Dredged material shall be placed within the channel adjacent to the jetty. The transport distance to the designated placement area varies depending on dredge assignment but typically is within one mile of the dredge cut. The following will be the performance periods:Calcasieu River Bar Channel: 15 January 2027 to TBDPascagoula Harbor: 01 April 2027 to 30 September 2027Panama City Harbor: 01 August 2027 to 30 September 2027This solicitation is unrestricted. The contract issued will be Firm Fixed Price. This solicitation will be issued in electronic format only and will be available on or about 23 October 2026. The bid opening date will be specified in the solicitation when it is issued. No additional media (CD-ROM, floppy disks, facsimiles, etc.) will be provided. Paper copies of this solicitation will not be available. Other methods of requesting a package will not be honored. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the size standard is $37,000,000.00. title: Department of War Pharmacy Uniform Formulary Blanket Purchase Agreement/Uniform Formulary Additional Discount Program
description: The Department of War (DoW) is required by law (10 U.S.C. � 1074g) to establish an effective, efficient, integrated pharmacy benefits program for the Military Health System (MHS) which includes the purchase pharmaceutical agents. The law and implementing regulation (32 CFR Section 199.21) describe the process by which the DoW Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) Committee will consider the relative clinical effectiveness and relative cost effectiveness of pharmaceutical agents in a therapeutic class in recommending the selection of agents for the DoW Uniform Formulary (UF) and, for cost sharing purposes, the classification of a pharmaceutical agent as generic, formulary, Basic Core Formulary (BCF), Extended Core Formulary (ECF), or non-formulary (NF). Prior to the scheduled P&T Committee meeting, a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for pharmaceutical agents within Drug Classes identified for placement on the UF has been issued to obtain quotes from industry. REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. title: Calcasieu Bar River Channel, Pascagoula Harbor, and Panama City Harbor Maintenance Dredging
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC) requires a contract to provide maintenance dredging for (3) dredging projects. The areas of consideration for these dredging services are: Calcasieu Bar River Channel, Pascagoula Harbor, and Panama City Harbor.Calcasieu River Bar Channel: Work for the Calcasieu River Bar Channel will require one fully crewed and equipped self-propelled trailing suction type hopper dredge. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -45ft MLLW and place dredged material into the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Sites (ODMDS).Pascagoula Harbor: Work for the Pascagoula Harbor maintenance dredging will require a hopper dredge. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -46 ft MLLW and place dredged material in the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Site (ODMDS). Dredged material shall be placed within Pascagoula ODMDS. The transport distance to the designated placement area varies depending on dredge assignment but typically is within 3-5 miles of the dredge cut.Panama City Harbor: Work for the Panama City Harbor maintenance dredging will require a medium to small hopper. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -40 ft MLLW and place dredged material within channel adjacent to the entrance jetty. Dredged material shall be placed within the channel adjacent to the jetty. The transport distance to the designated placement area varies depending on dredge assignment but typically is within one mile of the dredge cut. The following will be the performance periods:Calcasieu River Bar Channel: 15 January 2027 to TBDPascagoula Harbor: 01 April 2027 to 30 September 2027Panama City Harbor: 01 August 2027 to 30 September 2027This solicitation is unrestricted. The contract issued will be Firm Fixed Price. This solicitation will be issued in electronic format only and will be available on or about 23 October 2026. The bid opening date will be specified in the solicitation when it is issued. No additional media (CD-ROM, floppy disks, facsimiles, etc.) will be provided. Paper copies of this solicitation will not be available. Other methods of requesting a package will not be honored. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the size standard is $37,000,000.00. Offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) in order to be eligible to receive an award from any Government solicitation. Call 1-866-606-8220 for more information or visit the SAM website at www.sam.gov. After completing SAM, in order to download documents contractors and their subcontractors must register at www.sam.gov. In order to locate solicitation, Contractors can go to www. sam.gov and search for the solicitation number.Contractors can register to be put on a plan holders list that others can access through the www.sam.gov website. It is the Offerors responsibility to check the Internet address provided as necessary for any posted changes to this solicitation and all amendments. Job walk will be conducted at 11am on Monday, November 23rd, 2026.� Participants will meet with Ross Manoukian and Moses Dominguez in Bldg. 63 at the VA Greater Los Angeles Medical Center, 11301 Wilshire Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90073. A location map is attached to this solicitation. Please reach out to Moses Dominguez at 310-904-4009 if you need to locate the meeting point. Please email ositadima.ndubizu@va.gov to indicate intent to participate 1.m. Company info and quote should be in the attached Enclosure 1 form. All other forms of offer will not be accepted. Your enclosure form and capabilities statement/experience should be sent in one email with 2 separate email attachments, or it will not be accepted 2. Statement of Work BACKGROUND. The purpose of this contract is to have a contractor provide training, maintenance, repair, inspection and cleaning of the VA WLA Solar PV inverters and arrays. Contractor shall provide all maintenance and services. The Contractor shall furnish all parts, labor, equipment, qualified personnel, qualified supervision, and transportation necessary. SCOPE. Contractor shall provide services as follows: Preventative Maintenance Service Description Service Frequency General Inspections: Visual inspection for signs of damage, overall wear and tear, module breakage, loose conduit, broken straps, etc. Sample check torque marks and tighten loose connections 2x/yr Electrical Inspections and Maintenance: Perform Check integrity of weather resistance (seals, hubs and weather stripping) Check electrical equipment housing for signs of corrosion Perform Infrared scans, as needed In Contract Year 1 only, four single-technician, one-day dispatches for labor only corrective maintenance as needed 1x/yr Inverter Inspections and Maintenance: Check integrity of weather resistance (seals, hubs and weather stripping) Check inverter housing for signs of corrosion Clean inverter air vents and heat sink clean filters Replace inverter filters in AE Solaron model 250, 333, 500 and Satcon model 75, 250 central inverters Perform Infrared scans, as needed 1x/yr Array Washing: Includes normally expected soiling conditions. Heavy cleaning, such as excessive soiling, debris removal, bird droppings and soot, not to exceed 10% of total array 2x/yr & Additional Upon request Carport Solar Panel Washing and Cleaning: Carport Solar Panel Washing & Cleaning to occur on a weekend. 2x/yr Vegetation Control: Remove or mow weeds and grasses located in accessible areas under the array. description: Project Title: Department Of Energy - National Nuclear Security Administration Joint Cyber Facility Project Location: Building 810, Denver Federal Center, Lakewood, Colorado 80225 NAICS: 236220, Commercial & Institutional Building Construction Estimated Price Range: Between $10 and $20 million 1. Project Summary: The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), intends to procure construction services for a design-bid-build project for the development of a Joint Cyber Facility (JCF) for the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) at the Denver Federal Center in Lakewood, Colorado. This requirement for a new turnkey JCF consists of approximately 23,688 square feet of combined office and support space, including approximately 16,000 square feet of finished office workspace and 7,688 square feet of existing mechanical and electrical rooms supporting the space. The project includes integration of existing equipment from a prior data center installation. The finished space includes a reception area, offices, conference rooms, hoteling cubicles, pantry, server room, and a large video conferencing room. Construction and tenant build-out will occur within an occupied facility, necessitating careful coordination with active surrounding tenants. Work includes, demolition, architectural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, telecommunications, audio visual system infrastructure, security infrastructure, equipment, and coordinating installation of system furniture components, all of which must strictly adhere to accreditation requirements and standards. 2. To receive a copy of the scope of work documents, offerors must first complete the provided CUI Information Request Form (Request for Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI)) and any required Business License Form and submit the completed/signed forms to the Contracting Officer at jamie.potter@gsa.gov. After submitting the required forms, offerors must request access to the controlled documents through SAM.gov. Offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for solicitation amendments and other official updates.

description: AMENDMENT 0001 - PLEASE READ CAREFULLY! The purpose of this amendment is to formally update the solicitation and extend the proposal submission deadline as detailed below: 1. Change Set-Aside Status: This requirement is hereby converted from a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside to Full and Open Compeition (Unrestricted). Offers from all responsible commercial sources (large and small) will be considered. 2. Extended Closing Date: The proposal submission deadline is extended from 26 October 2026 to 07 December 2026 at 1:00pm CST. 3. Restructured CLINs: The solicitation is updated from 7 CLINs to 10 CLINs to align one-to-one with the 10 Categories in the Purchase Description 4. NAICS Code Registration Instruction: Added explicit guidance requiring offerors to hold the associated NAICS code in SAM.gov for any Category they wish to qualify for (see updated Section L, Paragraph 4). 5. Subcontracting Clauses Added: Incorporated FAR 52.219-8 (Utilization of Small Business Concerns) and FAR 52.219-9 (Small Business Subcontracting Plan). All updated attachments (Purchase Description, Attachment 0004) are uploaded below. Offerors must submit their revised proposals in accordance with these updated terms. SECTION A � SOLICITATION EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 1. THREE-STEP PROCUREMENT FRAMEWORK The Government will procure the Rapid Acquisition Sustainment Program (RASP) supply requirements utilizing a three-step process: Step One (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation): A separate Pre-solicitation Notice will not be issued; this synopsis is combined with the solicitation on SAM.gov in accordance with FAR Subpart 12.6. Individual order-level Request for Quotes (RFQs) under this Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) will be competed exclusively within the qualified pool and will not be synopsized, ensuring rapid execution. Clauses are in effect through FAC 2026-01. The primary NAICS code is 332710 (Machine Shops; Size Standard: 500 employees). Other codes are listed in Attachment 0001 - RASP BOA Purchase Description, and the Product Service Code is 5340 (Hardware, Commercial). Step Two (Master BOA Execution): The BOA Request for Proposal (RFP) will be released once for qualifications. The Government will execute no-cost, multi-award BOAs to responsible offerors whose proposals are compliant with Section L and rated "Acceptable" under Section M. BOAs are valid for up to five (5) years. NOTE: This RFP is the only opportunity to obtain a RASP BOA. Proposals will not be accepted or executed at any other time. If a contractor wishes to participate in any future RASP orders, they must respond to this initial RFP. Step Three (Order-Level Competition): As recurring supply needs arise, the PCO will issue competitive, order-level RFQs to the BOA pool. To participate, contractors must hold an active master BOA as of the RFQ closing date. Orders will result in individual, competitive Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contracts (Orders) under FAR 16.703. 2. title: Demolition of an existing building, Site Improvements and construction of a Modular Office Building at the US Merchant Marine Academy Campus, Kings Point, NY
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New York District intends to issue an invitation for bid to award a construction contract for the design and construction of a modular office space located along Steamboat Road on the US Merchant Marine Academy Campus (USMMA) adjacent to 307 Steamboat Road. The project magnitude is between $1-5M.This project will be advertised as 100% total Small Business Set-Aside. Summary of Work: The project objective is to design and provide a turnkey modular office facility. The scope includes the design and construction of a new office space of approximately 5,700 square feet, composed of custom modular units. The facility will be a single-story complex with a u-shaped space opening onto a small deck. It will house open offices with cubicles, six private offices, two conference rooms, four single-user bathrooms, a kitchenette/pantry room, lactation room, storage closets, and a mechanical room. The project scope encompasses incidental demolition, site prep work, foundations, underground utility hook ups, and site lighting. The contractor will also be responsible for providing furniture, fixtures, and equipment based upon the drawings and documentation provided in the Specifications package. The building and site infrastructure are required to have a minimum life expectancy of 10 to 15 years. The contract duration will be 136 calendar days for the entire project with phasing work involved.
